analysis: Tying history and target embeddings raised macro validation HR@10 from the reported 0.370 to 0.4275 (+0.0575), exceeding the hypothesized 0.02–0.04 gain. It remains 0.0775 below the reported SASRec baseline of 0.505. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.530, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.385, Electronics 0.335, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.460. These results support shared item representations in this architecture, but do not establish why sharing helped or whether contextualization is beneficial. The host accepted the trial; allocated GPU time was 597.11 seconds. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: One independently trained ItemAttention network per category uses a single shared 96-dimensional history/target embedding table, positional embeddings, two causal contextual blocks with two heads and dropout 0.2, and candidate-conditioned attention pooling. Normalized contextual values and candidate embeddings produce compatibility scores with learned scales, recency decay, and jointly trained item biases. Training retains sampled softmax with 127 training-history-excluded negatives, the two-term embedding penalty, AdamW, clipping, and validation checkpoint selection. Each category predictor strictly loads one selected tied-architecture checkpoint. Synthetic checks cover embedding identity, unique optimizer parameters, zero padding behavior, and exact save/load prediction parity while preserving training RNG state.
